_meta.indication: Topical treatment of plaque psoriasis in adults

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group trial; subjects randomized 2:1 to tapinarof cream, 1% or vehicle cream once daily for 12 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years of age with plaque psoriasis, BSA involvement of 3% to 20% and a PGA score of 2 (mild), 3 (moderate), or 4 (severe)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving PGA “treatment success” at Week 12 (PGA score of 0 [clear] or 1 [almost clear] with at least a 2-grade reduction from baseline)
pivotal_trials.result: PGA treatment success at Week 12: 35% tapinarof vs 6% vehicle; difference 29% (95% CI 23%, 36%); relative risk 5.8 (2.9, 11.5); p<0.001

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, double-blind, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group trial; subjects randomized 2:1 to tapinarof cream, 1% or vehicle cream once daily for 12 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years of age with plaque psoriasis, BSA involvement of 3% to 20% and a PGA score of 2 (mild), 3 (moderate), or 4 (severe)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving PGA “treatment success” at Week 12 (PGA score of 0 [clear] or 1 [almost clear] with at least a 2-grade reduction from baseline)
pivotal_trials.result: PGA treatment success at Week 12: 40% tapinarof vs 6% vehicle; difference 34% (95% CI 27%, 41%); relative risk 6.1 (3.3, 11.4); p<0.001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥1%): folliculitis (20% vs 1% vehicle), nasopharyngitis (11% vs 9%), contact dermatitis (7% vs 1%), headache (4% vs 1%), pruritus, and influenza. Discontinuations >1%: contact dermatitis (2.9%) and folliculitis (2.8%).
target_moa: Tapinarof is a small molecule aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) agonist/modulating agent; activation of AhR downregulates pro-inflammatory cytokines including IL-17A and F, and upregulates skin barrier proteins including filaggrin

rems.type: No REMS required; risk mitigation measures beyond professional labeling and standard postmarketing surveillance are not warranted at this time.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee was convened because no efficacy or safety issues were identified that required input from Advisory Committee.

description.text: Added indication for topical treatment of atopic dermatitis in adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the additional indication of the topical treatment of atopic dermatitis in adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older.

basis.text: Application was designated Standard (not Priority) review.

summary.text: Standard-review, first-cycle approval of a 505(b)(1) NDA for a new molecular entity; approved for the topical treatment of plaque psoriasis in adults based on two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials, with no accelerated approval, breakthrough, orphan, or priority designations.

citations.quote: The Applicant, Dermavant Sciences GBM, submitted a new drug application (NDA) 215272, VTAMA (tapinarof) cream, 1%, under Section 505(b)(1) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for the treatment of plaque psoriasis in adults.

To establish the efficacy of VTAMA in the treatment of adults with plaque psoriasis, the Applicant submitted the data from two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials (DMVT-505-3001, henceforth referred to as Study 3001; and DMVT-505-3002, henceforth referred to as Study 3002).

requirement.text: Conduct an open-label, long-term safety and pharmacokinetic (PK) study in at least 100 pediatric subjects with plaque psoriasis ages 2 to <18 years, with exposure to tapinarof cream, 1% for a minimum of 52 weeks (deferred pediatric study required under PREA/505B(a)).

citations.quote: 4283-1 Conduct an open-label, long-term safety and pharmacokinetic (PK) study in at least 100 pediatric subjects with plaque psoriasis ages 2 to <18 years. Subjects should be exposed to tapinarof cream, 1%, for a minimum of 52 weeks.
Your deferred pediatric study required by section 505B(a) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act is a required postmarketing study.
